title: A broadcast whose first copy is exactly 30 minutes after a receipt is the fallback's position there, and is precise through a later copy
reasoning: ADR 0003 at bfe51aa records Casey's answer (issue #55 comment 6995037213, item 3): "A broadcast's gateway copies count as one position, timed by the first copy, precise if any copy qualifies." Its late-edge sentence: "At a window's late edge, a first copy just inside means the broadcast is read and counts as precise even when its only qualifying copy arrived just outside. The late edge is ... 30 minutes after the receipt for the fallback".

c53-r's broadcast, packet 53004, cell c20 at 20 bits, reached c53-h1 on the public broker at 23 10:50:00 (c53-m004) and c53-h2 on MeshSTL only at 10:50:30 (c53-m005). The copies share node, packet id and stored values, so they are one position, timed 10:50:00, and it qualifies under pos_04 through c53-m005 (20 bits, seen_meshstl true). The copies' gateways are not c53-g and the rows have no relay_node, so they are no receipts and make no candidate at c53-g.

c53-r also sent cell D (20 bits, 1000.3 m north of c20 by stored values) at 22 09:05 and c20 at 22 09:10, both public. Those two cells neither overlap nor lie within 40 m, so every receipt's 7-day look-back holds two positions that are not the same place: c53-r is not stationary at any receipt and takes the 30-minute fallback (lnk_02, step 5).

The receipts are at 10:20:00, 10:20:10 and 10:20:20. The broadcast, at 10:50:00, is 30 minutes, 29 minutes 50 seconds and 29 minutes 40 seconds after them, inside each window ("30 minutes and 7 days are both inclusive", lnk_02); c53-m005, at 10:50:30, is outside all three. No other position lies within 30 minutes of any receipt, so the fallback takes the broadcast at each and its cell c20 is every receipt's box. c53-m006 at 10:20:00 sits on the window's late edge.

c53-r is not stationary, so each receipt keeps its own box (step 6); all three use c20. c53-g is stationary on its 16-bit position of 22 09:00 at every receipt and on its hour box, g16. One box per end (step 8).

relayer_precise_source reads the positions in each counted receipt's 30-minute window and 7-day look-back (PLAN, Data model; c44). The covered cell c20 was sent in the broadcast, which qualifies through c53-m005, so the flag is true; the public c20 of 22 09:10 adds nothing.

Timed by its later copy, the broadcast would be at 10:50:30, outside every window: no receipt would have a relayer position, and lnk_02 would drop all three, leaving no link-hour. Counted copy by copy, c53-m004 at 10:50:00 would be the fallback's position at every receipt, with the same box, but c53-m005 would be read by none, so the flag would be false.
gateway_precise_source is false: c53-g's only cell has 16 bits and was sent on the public broker.

Every receipt is a direct hop (relay_node 21 is c53-r's own byte, lnk_01) and passes lnk_05 at 2745.603337 m from c20 to g16, boxes not overlapping. The hour has 3 packets: kept. Medians: SNR 5, 6 and 7 dB give 6.0; RSSI -90, -95 and -100 dBm give -95.0. position_uncertainty_m is c20's 22.734410 m plus g16's 363.750397 m, = 386.484807 m (lnk_05).
